skills.name: detect-overlapping-workstreams
skills.description: Check whether a Software Factory workstream duplicates one that already exists in the org - the same goal, the same repositories, or the same intake sources - and warn the user before the redundant work starts. Use when creating a workstream, or when asked whether a goal is already covered by an existing one.

skills.name: init

skills.name: migrate
skills.description: Take substantial work from an agreed plan to a verified outcome, including new products, migrations, and large changes. Use when the user explicitly requests the migrate skill.

skills.name: install-code-review
skills.description: Install and configure Factory Droid for automated code review on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket (Cloud and Data Center), or Azure DevOps (Services and Server). Supports single-repo setup or org/group/workspace/project-wide rollout across hundreds of repos. Use when a user wants to set up Droid review on their repositories.

skills.name: install-triage
skills.description: Scaffold a scheduled Slack triage automation, generalized to any company. Sets up a Python tool layer (run_triage.py) plus a HEARTBEAT.md agent loop that scans configured Slack channels for actionable messages, dedupes against a ticketing system (Linear or Jira), files tickets, and posts a run summary. Use when the user wants to stand up an automated triage bot.

skills.name: review
skills.description:
Review code changes and identify high-confidence, actionable bugs. Use when the user wants to:

- Find bugs, security issues, or correctness problems in code changes
- Get a structured summary of review findings

skills.name: install-qa
skills.description: Use when the user wants to set up automated QA testing for a project. Analyzes the codebase, runs a guided questionnaire, and generates a modular QA skill with per-app sub-skills, CI integration (GitHub Actions or GitLab CI), and a standardized report template.

skills.name: security-review
skills.description:
Security-focused code review using STRIDE, OWASP Top 10, OWASP LLM Top 10, and supply chain analysis. Use when:
- Reviewing a PR for security vulnerabilities
- Performing a security audit of code changes
- Identifying injection, auth, data exposure, and other security issues
- Running a full-project security audit reviewing every source file

skills.name: deep-security-review
skills.description: For security-focused audits only, not generic deep code review or PR correctness review. Correctness-first, depth-first security audit of a single repository. Invoked by /security-review when the user opts into "thorough" mode. Uses a heterogeneous multi-model jury (latest Opus + latest GPT + latest Gemini) when public model endpoints are available, and a documented single-family BYOK degradation in airgap mode. A protected line-anchor floor runs against every Pass 0 lieutenant-seeded candidate; vendor and ecosystem prior-art enrichments run only when public network access is allowed. A conditional escalation tier (dataflow + reachability, exploit construction, adversarial red-team disprove) fires on per-finding triggers. Produces FINDINGS.md, JUDGE.md, DASHBOARD.md, severity-sorted master list, and optional PoC + evidence artifacts for that repo. Never uploads or submits anything; all outputs local.

skills.name: incident
skills.description: RCA runbook for alerts. Given an alert link (or prompted to provide one), identifies the alert type, verifies tooling/auth, and walks through root cause analysis using deep research. Persists learnings to incident-guidelines for future reuse.
